basic.commercialTags.label: Core commercial tags
basic.commercialTags.placeholder: e.g. Comeback, strong conflict, maxed-out suspense, workplace maneuvering
basic.competingFeel.label: Comparable feel / familiar reading experience
basic.competingFeel.placeholder: e.g. A realistic workplace sense of pressure with a touch of dry humor and high-density relationship tension
basic.description: This only confirms the basic parameters that shape the whole book's reading feel. When unsure, keep the defaults and AI will keep judging from your starting idea.
basic.emotion.label: Emotional intensity
basic.estimatedChapters.hint: Used as a reference for the book's structural density and later volume and chapter planning; it is not a hard cap.
basic.estimatedChapters.label: Estimated chapter count
basic.estimatedChapters.largePlanWarning: We suggest trying a small scope first: review the plan and early chapter directions, then expand the output scope once it matches your idea.
basic.extras.description: You can skip this if unsure. Once added, AI will better understand who this book is for and what the first 30 chapters should give readers.
basic.extras.heading: Add readers & selling points
basic.first30.label: First 30-chapter promise
basic.first30.placeholder: e.g. The first 30 chapters must let readers see the protagonist secure a first-stage foothold, the core rival surface, the first strong reversal in the relationship line, and make clear the book only gets fiercer from here.
basic.heading: First set this book's feel
basic.pace.label: Pacing preference
basic.pov.label: Narrative POV
basic.readerChannel.label: Reader channel preference
basic.sellingPoint.label: This book's core selling point
basic.sellingPoint.placeholder: e.g. Every time the protagonist solves a real-world predicament, it leverages a larger chain of relationships and interests, so readers keep anticipating the next counterstrike.
basic.targetAudience.label: Target readers
basic.targetAudience.placeholder: e.g. Readers who like high-pressure urban comebacks, relationship tension, and steady hooks that keep them reading.
candidates.heading: Direction candidates
candidates.subheading: Pick the direction closest to your idea first; if none fit, expand to adjust or generate another round.
controller.backgroundContinue: The director task will keep running in the background; you can check progress in the AI cockpit.

controller.createMainTaskFailed: Failed to create the director's main task.
controller.executeFailed: The director task failed to execute.
controller.generateIdeaFailed: Failed to generate the starting idea. Please try again later.
controller.needIdeaFirst: Please add a starting idea before generating or confirming a book-level direction.
controller.noResumableTask: There is no auto-director task to continue right now.

idea.confirmOverwrite: The starting idea above already has content. Use this inspiration and overwrite the original content?
idea.description: Write down the story you want to read, and AI will first organize it into selectable whole-book directions.
idea.inspirations.trigger: No idea? See a few openings
idea.placeholder: e.g. An ordinary female college student stumbles into a superpower organization; she studies and works part-time while investigating the truth of her father's disappearance.
idea.title: Start your whole book with one sentence
modelRun.autoExecution.heading: Execution scope & auto-approval
modelRun.autoExecution.hint: Takes effect only when you choose to execute by scope; it controls how far AI advances directly.
modelRun.autopilot.description: The system aims for the whole book, completing planning, chapter breakdown, prose generation, review, and repair. It only stops for an unavailable model, service errors, prose protection, or unrecoverable risks.
modelRun.autopilot.heading: Full-book autopilot
modelRun.description: Choose the model and automation scope for this run. Once confirmed, AI will generate the first batch of whole-book direction candidates.
modelRun.heading: Final check on how to proceed
modelRun.modelSettings.heading: Model settings
modelRun.modelSettings.hint: Uses the model selected at the top by default; expand to adjust when you need a temporary model swap.
modelRun.progressTarget.heading: How far should AI go this time
modelRun.progressTarget.hint: For a first run, we suggest generating directions and upfront planning first; once the approach is right, expand the auto-execution scope.
modelRun.runMode.auto_to_execution.descr: Choose the whole book, the first N chapters, or the first volume, and let the AI prepare and execute the target range directly.
modelRun.runMode.auto_to_execution.label: Execute by range
modelRun.runMode.auto_to_ready.descripti: The AI first prepares book-level planning, volume and chapter arrangements, and chapter-execution resources, then stops at the ready-to-write stage for your confirmation.
modelRun.runMode.auto_to_ready.label: Prepare until ready to write (recommended)
modelRun.runMode.auto_to_ready.recommend: We recommend checking whether the plan matches your ideas before producing chapters in bulk.
modelRun.runMode.full_book_autopilot.des: You only pick a direction at the start; the system plans, writes, reviews, and repairs toward the whole-book goal.
modelRun.styleReview.description: When enabled, once a chapter's prose is generated the system detects AI-tone risk and produces a revised draft when a fixable issue is found.
modelRun.styleReview.title: Post-prose AI-tone detection & fixes
page.restoreTaskFailed: Failed to restore the auto-director task.
page.subtitle: Start from one starting idea, confirm the default settings step by step, then choose a whole-book direction.
page.title: AI auto-director creation
worldStyle.description: You can pick a world sample for AI to reference, or let it organize this book's world automatically from your starting idea. The writing style becomes the default tone for later planning and prose.
worldStyle.heading: Give the story a world backdrop
worldStyle.mode.autoGenerate.description: Good for fantasy, xuanhuan, sci-fi, mystery, and other projects that need world rules to support them.
worldStyle.mode.autoGenerate.title: Generate this book's world from macro planning
worldStyle.mode.skip.description: Good for realistic themes and light-setting projects; characters and chapters advance mainly from the book-level plan.
worldStyle.mode.skip.title: No world setting for now
worldStyle.processing.heading: This book's world handling
worldStyle.processing.selectedWorld: The auto-director will reference the "{{name}}" world sample and, before character setup, organize the world constraints usable for this book.
worldStyle.styleField.defaultHint: When you have well-honed style assets, we recommend picking one directly to help you clearly anticipate how the director will write.
worldStyle.styleField.hint: Optional. Once selected, the director's first half reads only a lightweight style summary, and the prose stage keeps using the full style rules.
worldStyle.styleField.keywordsOnly: Use style keywords only for now
worldStyle.styleField.label: Book-level default writing style
worldStyle.styleField.summaryPrefix: This writing style shapes the tone and pace of later chapters:
worldStyle.worldField.hasWorldsHint: This only gives the auto-director a quick reference. Do full import, generation, and sync in the novel page's Book World section.
worldStyle.worldField.label: Reference world sample for planning
worldStyle.worldField.noWorldsHint: When no world sample is available, you can start the book with just your idea.
